findings.title: T-01 (tampering) — malformed payload validation
findings.description: POST /v1/tasks body validated by pydantic TaskCreate with blacklist + length cap.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: POST body with ";" returns 422 + problem+json via pydantic ValidationError. The handler also routes through pydantic's `extra='forbid'` so unknown fields are rejected. No reachable bypass.
findings.verify_evidence: Inline test_fr01.py:test_create_task_invalid_body_returns_422 covers 422 path. Pydantic raises ValidationError → service raises ValidationProblem → 422.

resolution.refute_evidence: taskq_api/models/schemas.py:48-55 rejects any blacklisted character via pydantic field_validator; api/tasks.py:38-43 calls tasks_service.create_task which wraps ValidationError into ValidationProblem. Verified via live repro: payload {"name":"a","command":"x; rm"} returns 422 + problem+json. Mitigation blocks the attack.

findings.title: T-02 (spoofing) — missing/forged X-API-Key
findings.description: X-API-Key missing or wrong → 401 + problem+json with identical detail.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: missing header → 401 with detail='missing or invalid API key'; forged hash → identical 401. No alternative path bypasses auth_dep because every /v1/* route declares it as Depends.
findings.verify_evidence: test_fr03.py unit cases cover both branches; live repro with arbitrary 'sk-xyz' string returns 401 with the canonical detail.

resolution.refute_evidence: api/deps.py:176-177 short-circuits on missing X-API-Key; _resolve_principal (line 119) chains lookup_active_key + auth_service.verify_key and re-raises UnauthorizedError on any mismatch. Detail string at deps.py:83 is identical across missing/unknown/revoked paths. Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-03 (spoofing) — API key stored as plaintext
findings.description: api_keys table stores only SHA-256 hex digest of plaintext; hmac.compare_digest on verify.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: created key with plaintext sk-...; row['key_hash'] equals sha256 hex (64 chars), plaintext absent from db. verify_key uses hmac.compare_digest (service/auth.py:84).
findings.verify_evidence: Live repro: row key_hash length 64, digest matches hashlib.sha256(plaintext), plaintext substring absent from raw db row.

resolution.refute_evidence: key_repo.py:117 writes only _hash(plaintext); service/auth.py:84 uses hmac.compare_digest for constant-time verification. Verified end-to-end via live create+inspect: row['key_hash'] == sha256(plaintext), plaintext not in row. Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-04 (elevation_of_privilege) — read key performs write/admin
findings.description: check_scope enforces read<write<admin before handler dispatches.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: read key + DELETE /v1/tasks/{id} → 403 with 'insufficient scope'. check_scope is invoked inside every handler before any resource lookup (api/tasks.py:40,51,63,76,86,96; api/metrics.py:43).
findings.verify_evidence: test_fr04.py:84 (test_sec_t04_write_key_cannot_delete) covers this; live repro of read-key on delete returns 403 before any service call.

resolution.refute_evidence: api/deps.py:194 compares via auth_service.scope_satisfies (service/auth.py:131) which is read<write<admin ranked. Every /v1 route calls check_scope before any repository action. Live repro: read key + DELETE → 403 with 'insufficient scope'. Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-05 (information_disclosure) — 403 reveals resource existence
findings.description: scope check fires before resource lookup; 403 body identical for existing/missing ids.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: DELETE /v1/tasks/{existing_id} and DELETE /v1/tasks/{missing_id} with a read-scope key both return 403 with detail='insufficient scope' and identical body (no path echo because problem_instance returns "" for 403).
findings.verify_evidence: test_spec_nfr.py:215 test_403_body_no_resource_leak asserts existing_body == missing_body. Live repro confirms byte-identical 403 envelopes.

resolution.refute_evidence: api/deps.py:88 _FORBIDDEN_DETAIL is a constant; api/deps.py:241-242 problem_instance returns "" for status 403 (no path echo). Verified live: 403 envelopes for existing vs missing task ids are byte-identical. Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-06 (elevation_of_privilege) — command injection via shell
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: grep for shell=True / eval( / exec( across 03-development/src returns 0 hits (test_spec_nfr.py:175-190 enforces this). create_subprocess_exec takes argv; shlex.split does not invoke a shell.
findings.verify_evidence: Static grep test_grep_shell_eval_exec_zero_hits passes; create_subprocess_exec never has shell=True.

resolution.refute_evidence: service/runner.py:126 uses asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with the splitted argv — no shell involved. Source-wide grep for shell=True / eval( / exec( returns zero hits (test_spec_nfr.py:175-190). Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-07 (denial_of_service) — subprocess hangs forever
findings.description: asyncio.wait_for(process.communicate(), timeout=TASKQ_TASK_TIMEOUT); on timeout → process.kill() + await process.wait().
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: patched _task_timeout=1.0, ran 'sleep 5'. Elapsed 1.01s; returned _ProcessResult(exit_code=None, stderr=''). No orphan process (verified via _reap_process calling process.kill() + await process.wait()).
findings.verify_evidence: Live repro: hung child killed within 1.01s budget; ps confirms no leftover sleep process.

resolution.refute_evidence: service/runner.py:135 wraps process.communicate in asyncio.wait_for(timeout=_task_timeout()); lines 138-140 call _reap_process which invokes process.kill() and awaits process.wait(). Live repro: 'sleep 5' with timeout=1.0s returns exit_code=None in 1.01s; no orphan. Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-08 (tampering) — SQL injection via string concatenation
findings.description: Repository uses ORM with bind parameters; the two text() calls in session.py are static.
findings.code_snippet:
result = connection.execute(text("SELECT 1"))
result.scalar()
...
row = connection.execute(
    text("SELECT version_num FROM alembic_version")
).first()
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: created task with name="evil'; DROP TABLE tasks; --"; all 3 rows persisted with the literal string in the name column. SQLAlchemy bind-parameterised the value; no concatenation.
findings.verify_evidence: test_grep_string_concat_sql_zero_hits in test_spec_nfr.py:193 enforces this; live repro confirms name with SQL meta-characters is stored as data, not interpreted.

resolution.refute_evidence: task_repo.create_task uses ORM session.add(Task(name=name)); session.flush emits INSERT with bind parameters. The two text() calls in session.py are static literals (no interpolation). Live repro: name="evil'; DROP TABLE tasks; --" stored as literal — 3 rows persisted, no drop. Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-09 (repudiation) — transaction boundary lost on exception
findings.description: session_scope commits on clean exit, rolls back on Exception, re-raises.
findings.code_snippet:
try:
    yield session
    session.commit()
except Exception:
    session.rollback()
    raise
finally:
    session.close()
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: opened session_scope, created 2 rows, raised RuntimeError mid-context; outer verify-scope SELECT shows 0 rows. Clean exit commits; exception path rolls back + re-raises.
findings.verify_evidence: test_fr09.py test_session_scope_rolls_back_on_exception (line 575) covers this; live repro shows zero rows after mid-context RuntimeError.

resolution.refute_evidence: session.py:179-181 catches Exception → rollback → raise. Live repro: 2 creates inside session_scope, mid-context RuntimeError raised, subsequent fresh session returns [] for tasks table. Cancellation propagates via BaseException, which intentionally passes through (NFR-03 contract). Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-10 (information_disclosure) — redact() helper missing despite NFR-04 declaration
findings.description: SAD §4 NFR-04 declares 'errors.redact() applied to all log handlers and metrics output'. No redact() function exists in 03-development/src; the only test (test_db_url_password_not_logged_unit) is a static grep that checks no source line passes db_url()/TASKQ_DB_URL into a logger. Current access logger (app.py:180) only logs method, path, status, correlation_id, so the practical leak surface is narrow.
findings.code_snippet: [NFR-04 spec gap] errors.py has no redact() function. grep -RIn 'def redact' over 03-development/src returns 0 hits.
findings.reasoning: Static evidence: source tree contains no redact() implementation; NFR-04 references it. Currently the access logger at app.py:180 only emits ('method path status correlation_id') so neither X-API-Key nor DB URL is logged. /v1/metrics returns only task_count and tasks_by_status dict. There is therefore no currently reachable exploit path, but the design contract is unenforced — a future log line that stringifies a request header or an exception repr would leak. The static-grep test in test_spec_nfr.py:374 enforces a narrow invariant (no db_url() inside a log call) but does not cover secrets held in variables.
findings.suggested_fix: Add errors.redact(s: str) -> str that masks (sk-..., Bearer ..., postgres(ql)://...:***@) and pipe it through the access logger and any other log formatter; back with a test exercising a logger.info('...{api_key}...') call to lock the invariant in.
findings.verify_evidence: grep -RIn 'def redact' over 03-development/src returns 0 hits. The access logger line at app.py:180 is the only place that would naturally need it and currently does not interpolate any secret. /v1/metrics body contains only task counts (api/metrics.py:53-57).

resolution.refute_evidence: While errors.redact() is not implemented (specification gap), no currently reachable code path leaks a secret. The access logger (app.py:180) only stringifies method/path/status/correlation_id; /v1/metrics body contains only task counts (api/metrics.py:54-57). The static-grep test at test_spec_nfr.py:374 enforces no db_url() inside a log call. Treated as documentation gap, not an active vulnerability — recorded as medium per severity rubric (defensive absence without reachable exploit).

findings.title: T-11 (information_disclosure) — 500 body leaks stack/SQL/path
findings.description: app.create_app registers Exception handler that returns fixed 'an internal error occurred' detail.
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: monkeypatched tasks_service.list_tasks to raise RuntimeError carrying stack/SQL/path text. Response body contained none of ('Traceback', 'SELECT', '/Users/', 'task_repo.py').
findings.verify_evidence: test_fr10.py test_500_body_no_stack_or_path (line 249) and test_spec_nfr.py test_500_body_no_leak (line 244) both cover this; live repro shows clean 500 envelope.

resolution.refute_evidence: app.py:230 hard-codes detail='an internal error occurred'; asyncio.CancelledError is re-raised (line 219-220) per NFR-03. Live repro: injected RuntimeError containing 'Traceback SELECT /Users/... task_repo.py' → 500 envelope contains none of those substrings. Mitigation effective.

findings.title: T-12 (denial_of_service) — per-token rate budget exhaustion
findings.description: Per-key token bucket with row-level lock; 429 + Retry-After.
findings.code_snippet:
with session_scope() as session:
    outcome = rate_repo.consume_token(
        session, key_id, bucket_size=burst, refill_rate_per_sec=per_sec
    )
findings.reasoning: Reproduced: seeded two api_keys (k1 with 0.5 tokens, k2 with 20). k1's 3 calls all 429; k2 admits successfully. Buckets are per-key_id, so an attacker cannot starve another client. with_for_update() at rate_repo.py:126 serialises concurrent refills on PostgreSQL (no-op on SQLite, which serialises writers at the DB level).
findings.verify_evidence: test_fr05.py:test_rate_limit_returns_429_with_retry_after and test_fr05.py:test_healthz_readyz_no_auth_no_rate_limit (line 311) cover this. Live repro confirms per-key isolation.

resolution.refute_evidence: rate_repo.py:126 uses with_for_update(); ratelimit.consume scopes one RateBucket row by key_id. Live repro: k1 with 0.5 tokens → 3× 429, k2 with 20 tokens → admit. Buckets are isolated per key. Mitigation effective.
